Since Putt became CEO this subverse has been dedicated to Voat as a whole as well as the glorious Putt, and a whole lot has happened with Voat in just a few days. Let's discuss it.

First we have Putt's announcement. A bombshell to many, but deep down we knew Voat's finances were not the most stable. I always struggled to believe that donations alone were supporting us. It turns out we had start-up grants, and that these have since run out. The tone of Putt's announcement was one of warning; an admission that Voat needs reliable and excess capital to not just survive but hire additional workers (as well as enable Putt himself to truly make Voat his work) and grow into something sustainable. He seemed to warn that finding an angel was the only real hope, and due to the totally real possibility that we might not be able to find one, people ought to prepare for a closure of Voat in the near future.

Putt's comments within the announcement thread were a little more optimistic. He mentioned being motivated by the donations received even at that time, and stated that it was not assuredly over. He summarized what Voat needs (operating costs covered, some investment for growth, and a staff), and mentioned he planned to reach out to free speech-supporting celebrities as a last ditch effort.

In the meantime I started a thread that I hope many of you have seen, attempting to document users who have seriously pledged to donate any amount to Voat monthly. The idea is that if we could get a list of dedicated goats with the intention to continue supporting Voat, we might be able to show that Voat can at the very least cover our operating costs for the foreseeable future. With only 55 users on the list at present, we already have close to $1000/month of the stated $6600/month present costs. I intend to expand this list as more goats who are donating monthly come forward and state that they are doing so.

Then reddit did what reddit does and violated freedom once more to the point that the majority of reddit's /r/The_Donald (at least those who already possessed accounts here, as we had a closure to account registrations at one point) was frustrated enough to make the move to Voat. In the past we've received bits and pieces of the 'pedes, adding to the 'pedes that largely made up Voat's userbase to begin with, but this is a substantially different occasion. A lot of users have come from reddit and, contrary to /u/Dumb_Comment_Bot's comic, most of them might actually stick around this time.

This is relevant for a number of reasons. Firstly, the finance aspect. More users means more bandwidth. One need only look at /v/all right now to see that there are numerous posts getting over 500 upvotes, which in the past was uncommon. If things stays this way it will mean more bandwidth for Voat.

That said, there have been claims that a substantial amount of money has already been donated to Voat since the arrival of these redditors. As for a source for these claims I cannot say, but if they are true it could mean great things for Voat's future. It could be enough to allow Putt and perhaps others to implement the changes necessary to sustain this platform going forward. There have already been some of the new redditors added to the list I posted above, showing that this financial support won't necessarily be a one-time dump, but may continue going forward.

Finally, Putt has said that he will provide us with an update over the weekend concerning the current state of our finances. Hopefully this will include more detailed information as to exactly where the monthly costs are presently coming from, as I know many goats have been asking for this. In the same comment he stated how he is humbled by the support already received, and that he was not expecting anything. This is reminiscent of Atko's response to the last donation drive or two. It must be something to do with being so personally aware of the financial state of Voat, but our admins don't seem to realize -- or at least they readily forget -- how much Voat means to so many people, and how willing we are to support it by whatever means necessary.

I think that's all I have to say for now. Sorry if this was a tad long. I'm less concerned than I was at the time of Putt's announcement, as his mood seems to have lightened somewhat (I'm sure we can make it through at least a few more months with what we've brought in already). I also eagerly await Putt's weekend update.

Stay vigilant.
